content.title: Leukoreduction by Manual Exchange Transfusion Versus Leukapheresis in the Management of Critical Pertussis in Children: A Case Series.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Marked leukocytosis in critical pertussis is a major predictor of mortality in young infants, with reported mortality rates of 40-85%. Although leukoreduction is frequently performed in critical pertussis with marked leukocytosis using either whole blood exchange transfusion or therapeutic leukapheresis, no evidence-based guidelines exist, and published data remain limited to small case reports. We present a descriptive case series evaluating the feasibility, hematologic response, and short-term outcomes of leukoreduction using these two modalities. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of five children aged 3-52 weeks with PCR-confirmed pertussis having marked leukocytosis admitted to a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit between February and July 2024. Leukoreduction was performed following multidisciplinary consensus. Absolute and percentage reductions in white blood cell (WBC) counts were calculated using pre- and post-procedure values. Clinical characteristics, illness severity scores (PRISM, PELOD, PIM3), leukoreduction modality, and procedural complications were reviewed. RESULTS: Median WBC count decreased from 58 × 10⁹/L (range, 33-81.6) before the procedure to 18 × 10⁹/L (range, 13-41) after the procedure, representing a median reduction of 64.1% (range, 38.1-75.8%). In this case series, exchange transfusion was associated with a greater median WBC reduction compared with leukapheresis (71.4% vs. 56.8%). However, exchange transfusion resulted in a more pronounced median reduction in platelet count (79.9% vs. 44.7%) and a greater increase in hemoglobin (mean increase, 5.5 g/dL vs. 0.47 g/dL). CONCLUSION: In this case series, leukoreduction was feasible and produced immediate cytoreduction in critically ill infants with pertussis-associated hyperleukocytosis. Exchange transfusion was associated with greater WBC reduction but more pronounced platelet depletion. Larger multicenter studies are needed to further evaluate these modalities and guide modality selection and timing.
